summary: M.S. Computer Engineering candidate at Rochester Institute of Technology with hands-on embedded C/C++ development across STM32 Cortex-M4, FreeRTOS-based real-time systems, and bare-metal peripheral drivers. Designed and debugged interrupt-driven firmware for sensor integration and motor control; proficient in UART/I2C/SPI communication protocols and hardware verification using Proteus simulation.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi Pico over SPI and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via embedded C/C++.
Implemented tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; performed root-cause analysis on sensor jitter and resolved via software calibration and ADC resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary — Robotics
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback on Arduino.
Led a 25-member team across 10+ national-level competitions; ranked 10th at Robocon among 45 universities.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a PyQt/Matplotlib GUI for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization; used GitLab for version control and collaborative technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on Cortex-M4; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified timing in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture with a low-level I2C driver; debugged interrupt priority conflicts through register-level inspection.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across UART command parsing, PWM servo control, and VL53L0X ToF sensing on STM32.
Implemented interrupt-driven UART command reception and multi-servo PWM control; resolved servo crosstalk through PWM timing analysis.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm — MS Capstone (COFFIN)
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection using dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Resolved 11 integration failures (servo crosstalk, rolling-shutter stereo depth, false-positive detections) through systematic root-cause analysis; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation - 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
1st Prize, CanSat Workshop - Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon - National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
